methodologyNotes: Adversarial re-verification pass. Every figure was re-read off the vendor's own live page on 2026-09-10, and in addition each page's RAW HTML was downloaded and grepped for currency symbols so that a silently client-rendered or missing price could not pass as a confirmed one: ezyvet.com/pricing/us (exactly one currency match, $260.50), provet.com/pricing ($0/$40/$99/$129/$249/$299 plus GBP), digitail.com/plans (ZERO currency matches across 600KB - the absence of prices is deliberate, not a rendering failure), vetport.com/pricing plus vetport.com/faqs, navetor.com/pricing ($0/$200/$300/$350/$400/$550), onwardvet.com/pricing ($300 only), daysmart.com/vet/pricing ($123 only), shepherd.vet, vetspire.ai, and go.covetrus.com/why-pulse-cloud-veterinary-software. Month-to-month vs annual was checked on every priced vendor: not one of these vendors publishes an annual-billing toggle or an annual discount, so no annual rate is sitting in a monthly field. DaySmart's $123 is confirmed monthly by the page's own JSON-LD UnitPriceSpecification (unitText MONTH, unitCode MON); VETport's $229 carries no frequency label on the pricing page at all and is confirmed monthly only by the FAQ's "All the plans of VETport are of monthly basis. There is no option for Annual Subscription". Per-vet, per-seat and per-location rates are kept in notes and never folded into monthlyUsd; Provet's monthlyUsd is the platform fee (the true single-vet floor), with the per-vet rate in notes. HIPAA governs human health information and does not cover veterinary records; raw-HTML greps returned zero hits for HIPAA, SOC 2 and GDPR on all ten pages, so those fields are null everywhere. The only compliance claim in the vertical is Provet's "PCI level 1 compliance", stated about Provet Pay rather than the platform, so it is noted but populates no compliance field. Hippo Manager stays dropped - hippomanager.com now serves an Indonesian online-gambling page, not a vendor site - and ImproMed stays dropped because covetrus.com returns a 212-byte body and software.covetrus.com returns HTTP 403, leaving nothing official to cite. No further vendor was removed. Unsupported marketing claims that the draft had attributed to vendor pages were struck: Shepherd's "Shepherd Pay" and wellness-plan module (both absent from the fetched HTML) and Covetrus's "SOAP notes, 6+ hours a week" (the cited page's only quantified claim is a 30-minutes-per-day testimonial). accessedAt 2026-09-10 throughout.

The published string is "Get started for as little as $260.50 per month"; the page never states what the price is per, so no per-user or per-vet unit was inferred. Grep for HIPAA returned 0 and the only "SOC" hit was inside markup, not body text. Change from draft: added Vello to integrations (listed in the page's own integrations navigation).

plans.name: Cloud subscription (published entry price)

Two buyer traps: the monthly price explicitly does NOT include implementation or data conversion, which are "scoped based on the size and structure of your clinic" with the amount unpublished; and the contract is a six-month initial term followed by three-month rolling terms, so this is not cancel-anytime monthly. vendors.name: VETport
vendors.provenance: Re-fetched https://www.vetport.com/pricing and https://www.vetport.com/faqs on 2026-09-10. The pricing page computes its figure in a client-side jQuery calculator, so a plain fetch renders "$ 0"; the recorded numbers come from the page's OWN script, read out of the raw HTML: the branch `if (user <= 2 && location == 1) $(".price").text("$ 229")`, then `Base_Price = 229`, `Additional_Users_Price = (user - 2) * 112`, `Additional_Locations_Price = (location - 1) * 140`, all inside `if (user <= 10 && location <= 5)` with the else branch un-hiding "Get a Quote". TWO corrections applied on this pass. (1) UNIT: the calculator's own label is "No. of Vets", not users - the script variable is merely named `user` - so the increments and the cap are per VET. (2) BILLING FREQUENCY: the pricing page contains zero occurrences of "month", "monthly" or "annual", so the $229 is unlabelled there; monthly billing is established only by the FAQ, verbatim "VETport charges it's customer on monthly basis. All the plans of VETport are of monthly basis. There is no option for Annual Subscription or long term contract." The 15-day trial and the $49 online-booking charge are likewise quoted from the FAQ.

plans.name: Base subscription (up to 2 vets, 1 location)
plans.notes: $229/month covers up to 2 VETS at 1 location - the calculator's slider is labelled "No. of Vets". Beyond that it adds $112/month per additional vet (from the 3rd) and $140/month per additional location (from the 2nd), so 4 vets at 1 location is $453/month and 2 vets at 2 locations is $369/month. Hard ceiling: above 10 vets or 5 locations the calculator hides the price and switches to "Get a Quote". Monthly billing is confirmed by the FAQ, not the pricing page - the pricing page never prints "month" at all: "All the plans of VETport are of monthly basis. There is no option for Annual Subscription or long term contract." So there is no annual rate to confuse this with, and no minimum contract. Caveat: an "initial setup fee" exists - the FAQ says initial training and setup are included in it - but the amount is never published anywhere.

plans.name: Online Booking (add-on)
plans.notes: Published in VETport's own FAQ, not on the pricing page: "Online booking is a premium service offered by VETport ... This service is chargeable at $49/month." It must be installed from the VETport Marketplace. A buyer comparing the $229 base against rivals that bundle online booking is not comparing like with like. Not a standalone plan.

plans.notes: Quote-only by design: the calculator's own guard is `if (user <= 10 && location <= 5)`, and past that threshold it stops returning a figure and un-hides "Get a Quote" / "Contact Now". No published rate card above 10 vets or 5 locations.

The page states pricing "considers number of locations, users, and integrations" and that rollout is planned by region or wave.

plans.name: Universities & Institutions
plans.notes: Marked "Custom" - no price published. "Flexible, custom arrangements for universities, research facilities, and corporate R&D centers": custom workflows and templates, institution-level governance, integration with existing systems, scoping sessions, and custom roles for students, residents, faculty and staff.

limits: $300/month is a starting figure; the per-doctor and per-user scaling rates are unpublished
"Optional add-ons can be tailored to your needs" - add-on prices are not disclosed
Data conversion feeds into the quote but its cost is not disclosed
Group and institutional tiers are entirely quote-based
No integration partners named on the pricing page; no free trial published
keyFeatures: AI note-taking and automation included in the base clinic plan
Institution tier with institution-level governance and custom roles for students, residents and faculty
Multi-location dashboards and standardized reporting for hospital groups, pitched as reducing overlapping third-party systems
bestFor: Single-location independent clinics wanting AI documentation included in the base price
Universities, research facilities and corporate R&D centers needing custom workflows and governance
enrichment.provenance: Official pricing page fetched and currency-grepped ($300 is the only figure). The institutional audience was corrected to the page's own wording and the unpriced optional add-ons were added; fields the page does not state are left null or empty.
